newsitem.title: ITALY: Credito stock soars on Goldman upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Credito stock soars on Goldman upgrade.

text.p: Credito Italiano stock soared to four-year highs on the Milan stock market after Goldman Sachs raised the bank to its European priority list from a market outperformer, a rating placed on the bank in January.
At 1110 GMT, Credito shares were trading 2.85 percent higher at 2,710 lire after touching a high of 2,715, a level not seen since the summer of 1993, in volume of over 17 million shares.
Dealers said the stock was seeing a lot of foreign investor buying interest on a generally firmer Milan bourse.

Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Crowder told Reuters that the bank's restructuring process should guarantee an improvement in its profit performance, adding that the share price had the potential to rise to 3,500 lire.
Crowder saw as very positive the bank's commitment to diversify its activities towards sectors of higher added-value like managed savings and insurance.

He also cited Credito's cost-cutting measures and its shift in loans policy towards medium-sized corporate clients which guaranteed higher margins, as well as growth in the bank's market share of deposits.
The analyst declined to speculate on the possibility of Credito acquiring other banks but said a greater consolidation of the Italian banking sector was probable.
